title: Bestiary
subtitle: Birds never talk much. They only sing of spring, of tears about to fall, and of poetry.

trails.title: A Colorful Story
trails.description: She wrote everything down to remember those unexpected yet beautiful days.

content.text:
March ■■
Good heavens! I never thought linear perspective would be so hard to learn. I asked plenty of dumb questions, but Uccello answered all of them patiently and kept encouraging me.
Father said I needed more practice too.

March ■■
The lords kept throwing out new ideas, but Uccello always managed to talk them down. The fresco is getting more and more lively and artistic ... It is an honor to witness the birth of a masterpiece.

March ■■
Following Uccello's advice, everyone tried that magical paint, including the most stubborn ones among us.
I hope these days never end.

April ■■
We are being dismissed.
My skills have improved over these last few days. Uccello generously shared his paint with us before he left.
The story is coming to an end. We have to leave the painting unfinished ...
I've put away the paint, but its odor remains in my mind.

items.text: Chamber Entrance, Cathedral Interior

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: *snore*

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Uccello.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Huh?! Who? Where?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh, s-sorry, I hadn't meant to drift to sleep. It's just that so much has happened over the past few days.
The Assassin's attention is fixed intently on the fresco before him.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Perhaps the bird in the fresco represents Uccello himself.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: "Uccello" means bird, after all.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Hmm ... so then in these paintings, Uccello is a wondrous bird that has many followers?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: A metaphor.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: It seems like we're nearly there, but something's still missing. Perhaps I can take a closer look.
APPLe slowly floats upward to the blank area.
As if in perfect synchronization, a beam of light passes through the stained glass, illuminating APPLe and the blank area before him.
Fervent reds, vivid greens ... a panoply of new colors blossom in the light, only to fade like the ebbing tide.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: You saw that too, right?
Ezio nods.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: There were colors—fleeting, yes, but no trace of color is ever fully erased. Let's see ...
Ezio wipes the blank section of the wall, then sniffs his hand.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: There's a faint metallic smell.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Metallic smell? But this APPLe doesn't see anything on the wall that could create such a smell.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Trust me, in my line of work, I've become very familiar with the scent.
There is unwavering confidence in his tone.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Erhm ... I do hope you aren't implying that those awful rumors that Mr. Leonardo told me yesterday are true.
"Then they cut their wrists to shed blood; mixed it with hair and soil and painted the mixture on the wall."

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: No, no-no-no-no-no, I refuse to follow this train of thought. It must be something else, something less gory; give me a minute ...

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Metal, oxidation, frescoes, and pigment ...
A series of keywords emerge and intertwine in his mind until the final piece of the puzzle falls into place.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Oh, I've got it!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Many artists in this era use pigments derived from minerals such as ochre, lapis lazuli, and chromium compounds.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: When exposed to moisture, they undergo oxidation, which may be the source of this metallic scent.
APPLe stares at the blank space in front of him.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Yes, it all makes sense now. I've cracked the code to this perplexing riddle, and the answer shines brighter than ever before—
A deliberate pause, as if awaiting thunderous applause from his audience.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Please.
The Assassin stifles a laugh and makes a polite bow to suggest he continue.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Ahem ... I can only conclude that the artists used a special pigment that's only visible under specific lighting!

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Only visible under specific lighting? How? That sounds like sorcery.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: This isn't sorcery, friend. It's science!

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Back in this APPLe's timeline—I mean homeland—pigments like this are not particularly rare.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: But why does this phenomenon seem to be receptive to ... my body ...? Oh, I see!
APPLe's golden glow grows even brighter, like a small rising sun.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: So this APPLe is no different than a kind of optical filter!

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: An optical filter?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: As you might know, sunlight consists of various wavelengths of electromagnetic radiation.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Waves of sunlight? I don't get it.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Erhm ... Never mind that; let's assume this pigment is only visible under specific colors of light, say, red light or orange light.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: At dusk, when the sun is near the horizon, its rays travel through the atmosphere at a steeper angle, which diffuses the blue and ultraviolet light, causing the sunlight to appear more orange and red. A sunset, in other words.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Building on this, if we use an optical filter to block out even more blue and ultraviolet wavelengths ...

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: You may as well get to the point, Mr. APPLe, because you've lost me.
APPLe twirls excitedly in midair.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: With the right amount of red and orange light, the pigment on the wall should become visible!

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: But for how long? The light from before faded in an instant.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Well, that's true ...

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Highly limited in duration—and in size, too, nothing like the breathtaking display Leonardo demonstrated in the monastery.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: It may require a particular angle to achieve the desired effect. However, figuring that out will take some complex mathematical calculations ...
They both pause to examine the painting.
The white space remains undisturbed, impervious to its observers.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: So this is Uccello's final puzzle, huh?

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: All this has really piqued my curiosity, Ezio. What kind of man was this Paolo Uccello?

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I'm sorry. I can't even recall his face.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Though I'm not surprised by his use of riddles, if he is anything like the other artists I know. They all like hiding puzzles in their work; it's a means of protecting them from imposters.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I do know he had a passion for drawing birds. That's part of the reason they call him "Uccello."

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: You can tell from the meticulous detailing he painted them with.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Other than that though he was quite ordinary.
Not as lively as Leonardo, nor as eccentric as Brunelleschi.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Is that so ...? Yet this "ordinary" man had a mind as vast as the universe itself.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: Not only was he a legendary painter, but he was also a pioneer in perspective and lighting.

items.speaker: APPLe
items.text: The perplexing puzzles he left in his works have proved an enduring challenge for scholars to decipher. Not to mention he seems to be one of these "Compliners" cultists!
Ezio doesn't seem to give the accusation much weight.
Reaching out his hand, he gently brushes the chipped wall.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: He was also a Florentine.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: And it's no wonder that a Florentine can work wonders.
The fog in the central nave has cleared.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Urgh ...
She awakens feeling like her body is filled with lead.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sotheby ... Leonardo ...

items.speaker: Leonardo
items.text: *snore*

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: *sob* Don't eat me, please ...
Vertin notices a half-open censer on the altar table.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: That must have been the source of the sleeping gas ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Thank you, Ms. Sotheby. That potion you gave me seems to have mitigated the effects of the gas.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: *sob* I'm not tasty, really ...
The sleeping young lady appears gripped in a terrible nightmare.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It seems they aren't going to be waking up any time soon.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Urgh ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: *pant* There you go.
The dozing duo are dragged behind the altar, hidden beneath the holy protection of its shadow.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: You should be safe here, for the time being.

items.speaker: Sotheby
items.text: Angel's trumpets are poisonous ... Keep clear from them ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... *sigh*

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I'm sorry. I'll be back as soon as I can.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Well, our reinforcements are in position.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: I understand that the Padre already took care of the rats in the central nave. You, go fetch them and lock them up!

items.speaker: Templar V
items.text: Yes, Commander!

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: The rest of you will follow me to eliminate our troublesome assassin, seize the Golden Apple and claim those relics!

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Now pull yourselves together! We can't let this assassin get the drop on us. So if I catch any of you slacking off, you're going to wish I'd kicked you off the ledge here.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Understand?!

items.speaker: Templar Knights
items.text: Yes, Commander!

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: May the Father of Understanding guide—hmm?
The Templar commander notices a slender shadow behind a brick chimney.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Who's there? Show yourself!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... Good afternoon, sir.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: You! Aren't you that visitor from last night?
A breeze sweeps through, carrying up the tension in the air.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Hmph, don't tell me; you snuck your way up here for some sightseeing, miss.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Get her!

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Hurry! Flank her from the other side!

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: She must be with the Assassins! Don't let her get away!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Urgh!
Obviously, these tiles weren't made for running.
Her foundation training didn't include any programs on rooftop evasion.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: I need to find Ezio and Mr. APPLe, but ...
The enormous dome looms ahead, the dark ventilation grates resembling the dim, watchful eyes of giant beasts.
Far from a welcoming sight.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: How should I get inside?

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: It appears you're lost, miss.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Thieves, courtesans, and foreigners ... I've always wondered why the Assassins only attract the likes of you as allies.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: It's not hard to side with the Assassins when the only other option is you.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Hah, you're just a band of faithless lowlifes, nothing more.
She inches backward but finds there's no more roof left to meet her step.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Do you cherish your life, miss? Or will you leap down like one of those suicidal assassins?

items.speaker: Templar Knights
items.text: Hahahaha!
Laughter erupts from the advancing thugs.
Her heart beats faster and faster, as if it might burst up from her throat at any moment.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Ughh!!
A throwing knife pierces through the commander's eye.

items.speaker: Templar Commander
items.text: Arghhh! M-My eye!!
Dead on.
Flashes of flying blades flicker in the chaos.

items.speaker: Templar V
items.text: Arrrgh!!
The Templars fall from the rooftop one by one.
Just around the corner, a grayish figure stands silently, like a phantom in the sunlight.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Ezio!

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: Follow the wall on the right until you see a mechanical bird. I placed it there to mark a hidden window. Your friend's waiting for you there.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: What about you?
The Assassin takes a step forward, directing his gaze toward another wave of Templars.
Their armor glints coldly in the waning sunlight, forming a restless, silver sea on the rooftop.

items.speaker: Ezio
items.text: I have other work to do.
